title: A flat local map with the same maximal ideal and residue field is an isomorphism on completions
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings and $\varphi:A\to B$ a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] local homomorphism ($\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$) such that $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and the induced map of residue fields $A/\mathfrak m_A\to B/\mathfrak m_B$ is an isomorphism. Let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m_A^n$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m_B^n$ be the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic and $\mathfrak m_B$-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with canonical maps $\iota_A:A\to A^\wedge$, $\iota_B:B\to B^\wedge$. Let $\varphi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ be the ring map $(a_n\bmod\mathfrak m_A^n)_n\mapsto(\varphi(a_n)\bmod\mathfrak m_B^n)_n$ (well defined since $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A^n)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^n$); it satisfies $\varphi^\wedge\circ\iota_A=\iota_B\circ\varphi$. Then $\varphi^\wedge$ is an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764); its proof uses Algebra Lemma 0394 (lemma-finite-after-completion), More on Algebra Lemma 0AGW (lemma-flat-after-completion), Algebra Lemma 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local) and Algebra Lemma 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated)

proof.text: Since $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ are finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $A^\wedge$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$ (the ideal generated by $\iota_A(\mathfrak m_A)$), equal to the kernel of $\pi_A:A^\wedge\to\kappa_A=A/\mathfrak m_A$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_1$, and $\pi_A$ induces $A^\wedge/\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge\cong\kappa_A$; likewise for $B^\wedge$, $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$, $\pi_B:B^\wedge\to\kappa_B=B/\mathfrak m_B$. By construction of $\varphi^\wedge$, $\pi_B\circ\varphi^\wedge=\bar\varphi\circ\pi_A$, where $\bar\varphi:\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$ is the residue field map, an isomorphism by hypothesis.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, setting (the completions are local with the residue fields of A and B)

proof.text: Since $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak m_AB$ we have $\mathfrak m_B^n=(\mathfrak m_AB)^n=\mathfrak m_A^nB$ for all $n\ge1$, so the inverse systems $(B/\mathfrak m_B^n)_n$ and $(B/\mathfrak m_A^nB)_n$ coincide and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m_A^nB$ is the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic completion of the $A$-module $B$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $x=(a_n\bmod\mathfrak m_A^n)_n\in A^\wedge$ and $y=(b_n\bmod\mathfrak m_B^n)_n\in B^\wedge$ we have $\varphi^\wedge(x)y=(\varphi(a_n)b_n\bmod\mathfrak m_A^nB)_n$: the $A^\wedge$-module structure of $B^\wedge$ via $\varphi^\wedge$ is the componentwise one of the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic completion of $B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, first sentence (B^ is the m_A-adic completion of B; Stacks quotes Algebra Lemma 0394 (1), which here is immediate from m_A B = m_B)

proof.text: $\varphi$ is a local homomorphism of local rings with $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ finitely generated (Step 1), and $B/\mathfrak m_AB=B/\mathfrak m_B=\kappa_B$ is a $\kappa_A$-vector space of dimension $1$, since $\bar\varphi:\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion] (2), $B^\wedge$ is a finitely generated $A^\wedge$-module via $\varphi^\wedge$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, first sentence (Algebra, Lemma 0394, lemma-finite-after-completion)

proof.text: $B$ is a flat $A$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-completion-flat] with $R=A$, $I=\mathfrak m_A$, $M=B$ (which contains the verification, made in the source, that $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(B,\kappa_A)=0$ because $B$ is flat, so that More on Algebra Lemma 0AGW applies), $\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak m_A^nB$ with its componentwise $A^\wedge$-module structure is a flat $A^\wedge$-module. By Step 2 this module is $B^\wedge$ with the $A^\wedge$-module structure via $\varphi^\wedge$, so $B^\wedge$ is flat over $A^\wedge$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, second and third sentences (Tor_1 vanishing and More on Algebra, Lemma 0AGW, lemma-flat-after-completion)

proof.text: $A^\wedge$ is local (Step 1) and $B^\wedge$ is a finitely generated (Step 3) flat (Step 4) $A^\wedge$-module, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] $B^\wedge$ is a free $A^\wedge$-module; being finitely generated it has a finite basis $e_1,\dots,e_r$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, fourth sentence (Algebra, Lemma 00NZ, lemma-finite-flat-local)

proof.text: The rank is $1$. The ideal $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge$ is the ideal of $B^\wedge$ generated by $\varphi^\wedge(\iota_A(\mathfrak m_A))=\iota_B(\varphi(\mathfrak m_A))$, which generates the same ideal as $\iota_B(\mathfrak m_B)$ because $\mathfrak m_B=\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)B$; so $(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge=\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] applied to $B$ and the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak m_B$, $\pi_B$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$, so $\pi_B$ induces $B^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge\cong\kappa_B$. This is an isomorphism of $A^\wedge/\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge\cong\kappa_A$-vector spaces, $\kappa_B$ being a $\kappa_A$-vector space through $\bar\varphi$, because $\pi_B(\varphi^\wedge(x)y)=\bar\varphi(\pi_A(x))\pi_B(y)$ (Step 1). As $\bar\varphi$ is an isomorphism, $\dim_{\kappa_A}B^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge=1$. On the other hand, from the basis of Step 5, $B^\wedge/(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge\cong(A^\wedge/\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)^r\cong\kappa_A^r$. Hence $r=1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, fifth sentence (kappa(m_A) = A^/m_A A^ -> B^/m_A B^ = B^/m_B B^ = kappa(m_B), using Algebra, Lemma 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated)

proof.text: So $B^\wedge=A^\wedge e$ is free with basis one element $e$. Write $1_{B^\wedge}=ue$ with $u\in A^\wedge$. If $u\in\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$ then $1\in(\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge)B^\wedge=\ker\pi_B$ (Step 6), contradicting $\pi_B(1)=1\neq0$; so $u$ is not in the maximal ideal of the local ring $A^\wedge$ (Step 1) and is a unit. Hence $1_{B^\wedge}=ue$ is also a basis of $B^\wedge$: every $y\in B^\wedge$ is $y=x\cdot1=\varphi^\wedge(x)$ for exactly one $x\in A^\wedge$. Thus the ring map $\varphi^\wedge$ is bijective, i.e. an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AGX (lemma-flat-unramified, line 10764), proof, last sentence (B^ free of rank 1, hence A^ -> B^ is an isomorphism)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against More on Algebra 0AGX (more-algebra.tex line 10764) and kept. Proof written in 7 steps following the Stacks proof: local structure of the completions (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring, Algebra 05GI/05GG); B^ is the m_A-adic completion of B (immediate from m_A B = m_B, elementary); B^ finite over A^ (new node lem-weil-pbc-finite-after-completion, Algebra 0394); B^ flat over A^ (new node lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-completion-flat, More on Algebra 0AGW for a flat module, which carries the Tor_1 vanishing); free by the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free (00NZ); rank 1 via lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (05GG); conclusion that phi^ is bijective written out (the unit u). Tags 0394, 0AGW, 00NZ, 05GG, 0AGX verified in tags/tags. stmt_deps kept. No Lean in slopmaster2.

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Seven steps along the proof of 0AGX, three new nodes: the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring (05GI(1)/05GG: the completion of a Noetherian local ring is local with maximal ideal m R^ and the same residue field; AdicCompletion/LocalRing.lean:85, maximalIdeal_eq_map :95, residueField_map_bijective :151, verified) and two unsplit nodes for 0394 (finiteness after completion) and 0AGW (completion of a flat module over a Noetherian ring is flat over the completion, with the Tor_1 verification folded in since Mathlib has no Tor criterion). B^ is the m_A-adic completion of B since m_A B = m_B; finite then flat then free over A^ (lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free, 00NZ); rank 1 by 05GG and the residue-field isomorphism; the generator is a unit multiple of 1, so phi^ is bijective.

lean.statement: theorem flat_local_completion_iso {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (hflat : φ.Flat) [IsLocalHom φ] (hmax : Ideal.map φ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) (hres : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) φ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_comap φ).ge)) : ∃ (φhat : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A →+* AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B), (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A) (a : A), AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ^ n) a → AdicCompletion.evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) n (φhat x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ n) (φ a)) ∧ Function.Bijective φhat ∧ φhat.comp (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)) = (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B)).comp φ
